steps: Add tests/test_blueprint_files.py that discovers blueprints/*.toml relative to the repo root
Assert the directory is non-empty, so the parametrized cases cannot silently collect nothing
Assert every file loads through swfactory.blueprint.load and declares a name and targets
Assert blueprint names are unique, since the name is the dag_id
Assert each stage order starts at intent and ends at deliver
Assert each sandbox ttl_s outlives the longest gate timeout
Run the target test command (factory.toml [commands].test) until the whole suite passes
tests: R1: test_there_is_at_least_one_blueprint - the glob is non-empty
R2: test_every_blueprint_loads - load() raises for no installed blueprint
R3: test_blueprint_names_are_unique - duplicate dag ids fail
R4: test_every_blueprint_loads - targets present, order runs intent..deliver
risks: A parametrized test over an empty glob passes vacuously; R1 exists to prevent exactly that
Resolving blueprints/ relative to the working directory instead of the module would break in a work cell; the module uses Path(__file__).parents[1]
Scope creep into changing a blueprint to satisfy a new assertion; the plan touches one new test file and nothing else
